tasks.task: Write help articles from support tickets

items.when: When you have a pile of tickets, to rank the questions by how often they come up
When you know the top questions and need articles written in the customer's words
When one solved ticket should become a page with steps and what the reader should see
When a page opens with background, to compare a version that gives the answer first
When a draft uses the team's inside words instead of the words customers type

tasks.task: Write a README and setup guide for a project

items.when: When you get a codebase with no docs and need a guided run from code read to tested README
When only one person knows how the project runs and the facts must be asked out of them
When you have the code, scripts and config and need a README a new developer can follow
When the project is public and the README must also make a stranger want to try it
When the README is drafted, to run each step and mark it working or broken with proof
When setup needs ten manual steps and some should be scripted, not documented

tasks.task: Write an API reference from a spec or code

items.when: When there is no OpenAPI file yet and you need one made from the code before you write
When you have the spec, examples and error list and need a reference that works first try
When the error list only gives codes, to say what went wrong and what to do next
When every example must be proven, to plan test calls with edge and failure cases
Before you publish, to list claims that have drifted from what the code does

tasks.task: Write a quickstart that gets a developer to a first call

items.when: Before writing, to find which sign-up and key steps slow a developer's first working call
When you know the shortest path and need the quickstart with copy-ready examples
When you want a second plan to compare: quickstart, tutorial and a sample app
When the quickstart is drafted, to follow it on a clean machine and log what breaks

tasks.task: Write an FAQ page for a product or shop

items.when: When the answer to a question is buried in old tickets and docs and must be found first
When you have real questions and the owner's answers and need one findable FAQ page
When some answers are too long for an FAQ and need their own article
When the product is new and has no tickets yet, to predict the hard questions people will ask
When the page is drafted, to put each answer first and list facts that still need a source

tasks.task: Write a user manual for a physical product

items.when: When the engineer holds the facts, to send questions aimed at what only they know
When you have specs, a parts list and support questions and need the full manual
When an illustrator or photographer must make the step pictures and needs a clear brief
When users keep making the same mistake and the manual blames them, not the product's cues
When a wrong step could hurt someone and the warnings must come before the step, not after
Before layout, to catch part names used two ways, typos and jargon without rewriting

tasks.task: Write a quick start card, assembly steps or care card

items.when: When the product needs a one-page card or numbered assembly steps with a diagram brief
When the steps will not fit the card and must lose words without losing a step
When returns come from one wrong step, to make that step hard to get wrong
When the card will be translated, to cut idioms and long sentences first

tasks.task: Build a troubleshooting chart

items.when: When you have returns reasons, reviews and tickets, to rank the faults by how common they are
When you know the common faults and need a symptom, cause and fix table
When a table gets long, to try the same faults as a yes or no decision tree
When the product shows error codes, to explain each one and its next step
When the chart is done, to check each part and light is named the same way throughout

tasks.task: Write release notes and a migration guide

items.when: At each release, to run the docs steps in order alongside the code
When the only record is the commit history, to get a first sorted list of changes
When you know what changed and who must act, to write the notes and upgrade steps
When executives, engineers and customers each need their own version of the same release
When the API changed, to flag breaking changes the migration guide must cover
Before the release ships, to check the notes and docs match what is going out

tasks.task: Add docstrings and comments to one source file

items.when: When you must understand a file before you document it, read in order for a newcomer
When every public function and class in one file needs a docstring and no code may change
When old comments are wrong or noisy and need tidying with the logic left alone
When the comments are written, to find any that say something the code does not do

tasks.task: Write handover notes and a code tour for the next developer

items.when: Before writing, to get an ordered map of the code and what a reader must know first
When a freelancer or agency hands over and the next person must run it from day one
When the new developer needs a step-by-step tour that links real files and lines
Before handover, to prove the run steps work for someone who is not the author

tasks.task: Write decision records from notes and threads

items.when: When a choice sits in meeting notes or a pull request thread and needs a short record
When the owner can tell you the choice and you need the options they passed on written up
When nothing is written down and the reasons must be asked out a few questions at a time
When the records use project words a new developer will not know

tasks.task: Write a getting started guide for an app or service

items.when: When early tickets show where new users get stuck, to pick what the guide must cover
When you have product facts and user problems and need short numbered routines
When a page may not be read, to compare a short in-app tour that teaches the same steps
When the guide is drafted, to walk the product and fix steps and labels that do not match
When the guide assumes words a first-day user has not met yet

tasks.task: Audit existing docs for gaps, drift and stale pages

items.when: Before writing anything new, or once a quarter, to list what is missing, stale or doubled
When a feature changed, to trace which pages and steps the change made out of date
When one README or page is in doubt, to list false claims and weak spots
When developer docs need a standing monthly pass for stale pages and broken steps
When the docs are an internal wiki, to find pages with no owner and missing procedures

tasks.task: Review an API design from its spec

items.when: When you have the spec, to score naming, errors and consistency and flag breaking changes
When an endpoint is easy to misuse, to find the parts that lead to security mistakes
When the API will be public and needs a versioning policy, rate limits and contract rules

tasks.task: Run a monthly help centre review

items.when: In the first week of each month, for any business with a help centre or FAQ page
When the client wants the review to run itself from last month's tickets
When a chatbot answers from the help pages, to find the questions it missed or got wrong
When the month's tickets must be sorted into themes before you pick pages to fix

tasks.task: Plan a documentation structure and style guide

items.when: Before the plan, to see what exists and what readers cannot find
When a team asks what to write down, where it lives and who keeps it fresh
When the help centre needs a page tree, menu and links readers can find their way through
When several people write the docs and need tone rules, word lists and examples
When the same thing has three names across pages and one term must be chosen

tasks.task: Write a plain-language policy page

items.when: Before and after the rewrite, to find gaps, clashes and unclear wording in the policies
When the policy is correct but written in legal words customers do not read
When a vague phrase hides what the policy really does to the customer

tasks.task: Write a technical design document

items.when: When the design is not settled, to lay out the choice, diagrams and trade-offs first
When the engineers have decided and you must write it up for readers outside the team
When the document needs a flow or data diagram that lives as text beside the docs
When the explanation is correct but hard to follow, and one small worked example would fix it
When the document is drafted, to have it tested for hidden assumptions and ways to fail

tasks.task: Write an internal procedure or runbook

items.when: When a team's way of working must become a flowchart and a written procedure with edge cases
When one repeat task needs exact steps, fixes if it fails and how to roll back
When the team has no procedures at all and needs a system and the first set written
When procedures exist, to find missing owners, stale steps and gaps

tasks.task: Rewrite error messages and interface text

items.when: When an app's errors and empty screens need listing in full before any rewording
When error messages blame the user or give a code and nothing to do next
When labels and buttons need a friendlier voice, to compare with the plain version
When the new text is in place, to score the screen and rank what still confuses

tasks.task: Make diagrams and plan pictures for docs

items.when: When a flow or system should be a text diagram that can be pasted into the docs
When the page needs a clean picture file of a system or process
When a help page needs fresh screenshots of the product in a browser
When an illustrator will draw the pictures and needs one brief for the set

tasks.task: Plan how an API connects to another tool or AI assistant

items.when: When the client wants AI assistants to use their API and needs the steps and safety checks
When the plan is agreed and a first connector must be made from the API spec
When AI tools should find the right docs pages, to write the guide file that points to them
Before anyone installs the connector, to rank the ways it could be misused and the fixes

always.when: Before any doc is published, to list typos, term clashes and jargon without rewriting it
When a page is for customers and reads like it was written for the team
When a page states a limit, date, price or standard you cannot trace to the client's files
Before a doc is published, so a fresh reader with only the brief lists what they would still have to ask

helpers.when: When code samples or setup steps must be run and fixed, not only written down
When the manual or help centre must ship in a second language
When a manual or quick start card needs page layout and print-ready files
When the job needs ticket exports sorted or saved replies written to match the new pages
When a manual needs safety warnings, marks or legal wording checked against the rules
When the real fix is the screen or the first-use flow, not the words that explain it

gaps: No library item writes a user manual, quick start card, assembly steps or care card for a physical product; only the kit covers them
No library item writes safety warnings and hazard labels for a manual or checks them against product safety rules
No library item briefs an exploded diagram or step drawing, or plans and labels screenshots for a help page
No library item offers two or three structures for a manual, policy page or troubleshooting chart to compare
No library item tests customer instructions by following each step the way the first-run tester does for a README
No library item writes a migration guide or a deprecation notice; the release items stop at the changelog
No library item measures the reading grade of a help page or checks text is ready for translation
No library item finds broken links, old screenshots and out-of-date steps across a help centre
No library item writes a documentation style guide with a word list, heading rules and example pages
No library item sets up a docs site or a docs-as-code build; only the kit's release cycle covers the routine
No library item writes a plain-language warranty or terms summary; the policy items only check or draft legal text
